source_text: Dicunt etiam motum genitalium et commixtionem coniugum a diabolo fuisse repertam, et propterea eos qui nascuntur innocentes reos esse et a diabolo fieri, non a Deo, quia de hac diabolica commixtione nascuntur. Hoc autem sine aliqua ambiguitate Manichaeum est.
pass_a_gloss: They also say that the movement of the genital members and the mixing of spouses was devised by the devil, and that for this reason those who are born, though innocent, are guilty and are made by the devil, not by God, because they are born from this diabolical mixing. And this without any ambiguity is Manichaean.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: They also say that the movement of the sexual organs and the intercourse of married couples were devised by the devil. For that reason, they say, people who are born innocent are guilty and are made by the devil rather than by God, because they are born from this diabolical intercourse. This is unmistakably Manichaean.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (Letter to Rome, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 1); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
